advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make facade_function() raise (or log) instead of silently falling back to getattr(rebar, name) when no listed _FACADE_MODULES module defines the symbol, so a relocated/undiscoverable facade is a hard failure rather than a derivation from a possibly-patched namespace.
evidence: Docstring at :277 claims resolution 'from its defining rebar._lib_* module rather than the rebar namespace'
_FACADE_MODULES is a fixed 6-tuple (:264-271); a facade function moved to or newly defined in any other module silently takes the fallback and derives from the facade namespace
ABSENCE: no error/warning distinguishes 'resolved from the defining module' from 'fell back to the facade namespace' — the two outcomes are indistinguishable at the call site
advisory.finding: facade_function() silently falls back to getattr(rebar, name) when the library function's defining module is not in the hardcoded _FACADE_MODULES tuple. The docstring promises it resolves the signature from the defining rebar._lib_* module 'so a test that patches rebar.<name> before the server is built still derives the real signature', but the fallback path derives from the (possibly patched or relocated) rebar namespace instead — contradicting the stated contract and deriving the wrong signature without any error.
scenarios: A library facade function is relocated to a new rebar._lib_* module not listed in _FACADE_MODULES
A test patches rebar.<name> for a tool whose defining module is missing from the tuple — derivation reads the patched signature
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace the `return getattr(rebar, name)` fallback with a RuntimeError naming the symbol and _FACADE_MODULES, mirroring the deleted script's _facade_function which refused rather than measuring a stand-in.
